title: Frontend: Holy Grail
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Holy Grail. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Build semantic header, nav, main, aside, footer regions with texts Header, Navigation, Content, Related, Footer. Use a CSS grid that switches to one column below 600px without page-width overflow. Main content must allow shrinking via min-width:0.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use CSS Grid to express the desktop areas and a minmax(0,1fr) content track to allow internal overflow.
alternativeApproaches: Make the main region independently scrollable without trapping browser navigation or hiding the footer.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: 320px viewport; long code block; missing aside.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
